import FormalConjecturesUtil
import FormalConjectures.ErdosProblems.«246»

/-!
# Erdős Problem 1110

*Reference:* [Erdős Problem 1110](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1110)
-/

namespace Erdos1110

/--
$n$ is representable with respect to $p$ and $q$ if it is the sum of a finite
divisibility antichain of terms of the form $p^kq^l$.
-/
def Representable (p q n : ℕ) : Prop :=
  ∃ s : Finset ℕ,
    (s : Set ℕ) ⊆ Erdos246.Gamma p q ∧
    IsAntichain (· ∣ ·) (s : Set ℕ) ∧
    s.sum id = n

/--
Let $p>q\geq 2$ be two coprime integers. We call $n$ representable if it is the sum of
integers of the form $p^kq^l$, none of which divide each other.

If $\{p,q\}\neq \{2,3\}$ then what can be said about the density of non-representable
numbers? Are there infinitely many coprime non-representable numbers?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 5 11]
theorem erdos_1110 :
    answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ (p q : ℕ), q < p → 2 ≤ q →
      Nat.Coprime p q → ¬(p = 3 ∧ q = 2) →
      Set.Infinite {n : ℕ | Nat.Coprime n (p * q) ∧ ¬Representable p q n} := by
  sorry

end Erdos1110

findings.description: The condition `Nat.Coprime n (p * q)` interprets “coprime non-representable numbers” as numbers individually coprime to both bases. A natural reading of the source is instead an infinite family of non-representable numbers coprime to one another, requiring an infinite set satisfying `Set.Pairwise Nat.Coprime`. These conditions are not equivalent for arbitrary sets: `{n : ℕ | Nat.Coprime n 10 ∧ 3 ∣ n}` is infinite, but every pairwise-coprime subset has at most one element; this distinction was proved in Lean. This is not a counterexample involving `Representable`, and I have not established whether a special equivalence holds for its complement. Because the accessible sources leave “coprime” unqualified, this merits clarification rather than a definite misformalization finding.
findings.source_evidence: https://www.erdosproblems.com/1110 asks “Are there infinitely many coprime non-representable numbers?” Erdős–Lewin, “d-complete sequences of integers,” Math. Comp. 65 (1996), p. 840, likewise asks “Are there infinitely many coprime nonrepresentables?” Neither passage explicitly says “coprime to pq.” Original paper: https://www.ams.org/journals/mcom/1996-65-214/S0025-5718-96-00707-7/S0025-5718-96-00707-7.pdf.
findings.suggested_fix: Clarify the intended coprimality relation against the precise result in Yu–Chen (2022). If pairwise coprimality is intended, replace the final infinitude condition with `∃ S : Set ℕ, S.Infinite ∧ S.Pairwise Nat.Coprime ∧ ∀ n ∈ S, ¬Representable p q n`. Otherwise, cite a source explicitly specifying coprimality to pq, or establish the equivalence for this particular non-representability set.

could_not_verify: Erdos1110.erdos_1110: the intended meaning of “coprime nonrepresentables,” and any equivalence between the two readings for this specific set, remain unsettled. The original paper and website use the same unqualified phrase. Yu–Chen (2022) full text could not be obtained; its bibliography and zbMATH review were accessible but did not resolve this point.
review.notes: No confirmed mathematical defect was found in `Erdos1110.Representable`. The natural-number exponents, distinct finite summands, and divisibility-antichain condition match the original paper. Empty and singleton sums were checked; allowing the empty sum merely represents zero and does not enlarge the non-representable set. The parameter hypotheses are satisfiable, including composite bases, and the ordered exclusion `(p,q) ≠ (3,2)` correctly encodes the excluded unordered pair under `q < p`. The answer slot has the intended Prop type and global quantifier scope. The source still records the general question as open. Scratch files in /workspace/review/ compile successfully: computation.lean proves a finite-search equivalence with Representable for bases greater than 1, evaluates every n ≤ 20 for (4,3), (5,2), and (3,2), and proves small positive and negative instances. coprimality.lean proves the generic distinction discussed above. The named proof lemmas do not depend on sorryAx. The target file is unchanged. The density question and other remarks are not separately formalized in this file; that is a coverage limitation, not an additional finding.
